evaluation: First pass written by Claude (agent) on 2026-09-25 for the author's review. Values follow the Burra Charter's aspects of cultural significance: historic, scientific, social, memorial (spiritual) and aesthetic. Designations remain open to the people each site matters to and, in time, to the Moon's own nations.
reading_rule: Computed fields (heights, status, depth, pressure, distances, water body) come from the geography atlas at the scenario share; the evaluation fields are written judgment.

sites.name: Apollo 11, Tranquility Base
sites.marks: The first time people walked on another world.

values.historic: The first crewed landing and the first footsteps beyond Earth.
values.social: One of the most widely shared events in human memory, watched live by hundreds of millions.
values.memorial: An Apollo 1 patch and medals for Yuri Gagarin and Vladimir Komarov were left in tribute.
values.scientific: The first returned lunar samples and the laser reflector still used for ranging.
values.aesthetic: A small, legible scene: descent stage, instruments and footpaths within about 60 m.

sites.place_dependence: High. The meaning is the exact ground where the first steps were taken.
sites.survives: Descent stage, seismometer and laser reflector, camera, flag (blown over at lift-off), tools and discarded equipment, footprints and tracks.
sites.matters_to: People everywhere who count the first landing as part of their own story; the families of the crew; the community that will live with the site.
sites.proposed_treatment: Undersea domed community around the site. The footprint field and hardware are cut out into sealed trays at its heart; a tower and harbour mark the spot on the sea.
sites.reason: The place carries the meaning, and a living community keeps it cared for across generations.
sites.consult: Families of the crew; heritage specialists; the future resident community.
sites.open_questions: Design depth (466 m at 28%, built for about 700 m); how visitors reach the sealed core.

sites.name: Apollo 12 and Surveyor 3
sites.marks: A precision landing beside an earlier robotic lander, and the first return to a spacecraft on another world.

values.historic: Proved pinpoint landing; the crew removed parts of Surveyor 3 for study on Earth.
values.scientific: Surveyor 3's parts became the first study of hardware exposed on the Moon for years.
values.aesthetic: Two eras of exploration side by side, about 180 m apart.

sites.place_dependence: High. The pairing of the two landers at one spot is the story.
sites.survives: Descent stage, instrument station, Surveyor 3 (with parts removed), tracks between them.
sites.matters_to: People who follow the history of exploration; families of the crew; the community on the new coast.
sites.treatment_type: coastal site, undersea if the shore rises
sites.proposed_treatment: Coastal domed site built to become an undersea community if the shore rises.
sites.reason: It stands about 50 m above the 28% sea, within the shoreline's uncertainty.
sites.consult: Families of the crew; heritage specialists.
sites.open_questions: Final shoreline after groundwater uptake and crustal loading.

sites.name: Apollo 14, Fra Mauro
sites.marks: The first landing in the highlands of the Fra Mauro formation; the crew walked toward Cone crater.

values.historic: The return to flight after Apollo 13.
values.scientific: Samples from the Imbrium ejecta and Cone crater; the laser reflector that stays dry at 28%.
values.social: Remembered for the golf shots and for the walk up Cone crater.

sites.place_dependence: High for the landing site; the nearby young Cone crater adds scientific value in place.
sites.survives: Descent stage, instrument station, laser reflector, the handcart, golf balls, tracks toward Cone crater.
sites.matters_to: Families of the crew; people who follow exploration history; planetary scientists.
sites.proposed_treatment: Land heritage site with an enclosed core; candidate for the sealed reference area around Cone crater.
sites.reason: It stays dry with 436 m of margin, and Cone crater is young and already sampled.
sites.consult: Families of the crew; heritage specialists; planetary scientists.
sites.open_questions: Whether the reference area goes here or at Apollo 16.

sites.name: Apollo 15, Hadley-Apennine
sites.marks: The first lunar rover, the Genesis Rock, and the Fallen Astronaut memorial.

values.historic: The first long-range surface exploration by rover.
values.memorial: The Fallen Astronaut sculpture and a plaque naming 14 astronauts and cosmonauts who died.
values.scientific: The Genesis Rock and the study of Hadley Rille.
values.social: The hammer-and-feather demonstration of Galileo's principle.
values.aesthetic: A landing between the Apennine front and Hadley Rille, one of the most dramatic sites on the Moon.

sites.place_dependence: High. The memorial was placed on this ground by the crew.
sites.survives: Descent stage, rover, instrument station, laser reflector, the memorial and plaque, tracks.
sites.matters_to: Families of the crew and of the 14 people named on the plaque; people everywhere who follow exploration.
sites.proposed_treatment: Undersea domed community around the site, with the memorial kept in place inside; a related community can stand on the Apennine coast 8 km away.
sites.reason: Its memorial and landscape both tie it to this spot.
sites.consult: Families of the crew and of those named on the plaque.
sites.open_questions: How the memorial is shown so that it stays a place of remembrance.

sites.name: Apollo 16, Descartes
sites.marks: The only crewed landing in the central highlands.

values.historic: The first telescope operated from the Moon's surface, the far-ultraviolet camera.
values.scientific: Highland samples, including those from North Ray and South Ray craters.
values.social: A family photograph left by Charlie Duke.

sites.place_dependence: High for the landing site; the young craters add scientific value in place.
sites.survives: Descent stage, rover, instrument station, ultraviolet camera, tracks.
sites.matters_to: Families of the crew; astronomers; people who follow exploration.
sites.proposed_treatment: Land heritage site with an enclosed core; first candidate for the sealed reference area (North Ray and South Ray).
sites.reason: It stands 1,416 m above the sea, secure against any plausible shoreline.
sites.consult: Families of the crew; heritage specialists; planetary scientists.
sites.open_questions: The size of the reference area.

sites.name: Apollo 17, Taurus-Littrow
sites.marks: The last crewed landing to date, with the only geologist to walk on the Moon.

values.historic: The end of the first era of crewed exploration.
values.scientific: Orange volcanic glass from Shorty crater; the longest surface stay of the Apollo programme.
values.memorial: The plaque: 'May the spirit of peace in which we came be reflected in the lives of all mankind.'

sites.place_dependence: High. The valley and the plaque belong together.
sites.survives: Descent stage, rover, instrument station, plaque, tracks through the valley.
sites.matters_to: Families of the crew; geologists; people everywhere who follow exploration.
sites.proposed_treatment: Undersea domed community around the site; a related community can stand on the Taurus massifs 6 km away.
sites.reason: Its meaning is tied to the valley.
sites.consult: Families of the crew; heritage specialists.
sites.open_questions: The depth of 1,036 m (about 17 atm) makes the heaviest of the Apollo enclosures.

sites.name: Luna 2 impact
sites.marks: The first human-made object to reach the Moon.

values.historic: The first physical contact between human craft and another world.
values.social: It carried commemorative pennants, a first gesture of arrival.

sites.place_dependence: Moderate. The meaning is the arrival; the craft was scattered at impact.
sites.survives: Impact debris spread across the ground, still unlocated.
sites.matters_to: People who follow the history of exploration.
sites.proposed_treatment: A marker on the sea above the impact point, with any recovered fragments kept in a nearby undersea community.
sites.reason: This evaluation differs from the author's standing rule of a submerged community for every covered site, because little survives in place. The author decides.
sites.open_questions: Whether a survey can locate fragments before flooding.

sites.name: Luna 9
sites.marks: The first soft landing and the first pictures from the surface of another world.

values.historic: Showed that the surface could bear a lander.
values.scientific: The first close views of the regolith.

sites.matters_to: People who follow the history of exploration.
sites.proposed_treatment: Land heritage site with an enclosed core on the western coast of the Near-side Sea.
sites.reason: It stays dry, 393 m above the sea and 7 km from it.

sites.name: Surveyor 1
sites.marks: An early soft landing that returned thousands of surface images.

values.historic: Prepared the ground for crewed landings.

sites.matters_to: People who follow the history of exploration.
sites.proposed_treatment: Relic chamber or small undersea community under 377 m of water; scale set with the author.
sites.reason: It is covered by the sea; its story is mostly the craft itself.

sites.name: Lunokhod 1 and Luna 17
sites.marks: The first rover driven on another world.

values.historic: Ten months of remote driving across Mare Imbrium.
values.scientific: Its laser reflector, found again in 2010, is still used for ranging.

sites.place_dependence: Moderate. The rover's final resting place ends a long traverse.
sites.matters_to: People who follow the history of exploration and robotics.
sites.proposed_treatment: Undersea community around the rover's resting place, 864 m down.
sites.reason: The author's rule for covered sites; the first rover is a strong heritage site in its own right.

sites.name: Lunokhod 2 and Luna 21
sites.marks: A rover that drove about 39 km, the longest drive for decades.

values.historic: Long-distance remote exploration.
values.scientific: Its laser reflector is still used.

sites.survives: Rover, landing stage, tracks toward Le Monnier.
sites.matters_to: People who follow the history of exploration.
sites.proposed_treatment: Undersea community or a relic chamber tended from the Le Monnier coast 15 km away.
sites.reason: Covered by 1,140 m of water, close to a coast.

sites.name: Luna 16
sites.marks: The first robotic sample return.

values.historic: Proved sample return without crews.

sites.matters_to: People who follow the history of exploration.
sites.proposed_treatment: Relic chamber or small undersea community, 806 m down.
sites.reason: Covered by the sea.

sites.name: Luna 24
sites.marks: The last sample return for 44 years.

values.historic: Closed the first era of sample return.
values.scientific: A deep drill core from Mare Crisium.

sites.matters_to: People who follow the history of exploration.
sites.proposed_treatment: Relic chamber or small undersea community, 2,148 m down.
sites.reason: Covered by the sea.

sites.name: Chang'e 3 and Yutu
sites.marks: The first soft landing on the Moon in 37 years.

values.historic: Reopened surface exploration.
values.scientific: Ground-penetrating radar of Mare Imbrium's layers.

sites.matters_to: People who follow the history of exploration.
sites.proposed_treatment: Undersea community, 1,211 m down.
sites.reason: The author's rule for covered sites.

sites.name: Chang'e 4 and Yutu-2
sites.marks: The first landing on the far side, and the first seeds to sprout on the Moon.

values.historic: Opened the far side to surface exploration.
values.scientific: Radar and spectral study of the South Pole-Aitken basin floor.
values.social: Cotton seeds sprouted in a small sealed habitat: the first plant growth on the Moon, a fitting ancestor for a living Moon.

sites.place_dependence: Moderate to high. It sits in Von Karman crater on the floor of the Moon's largest basin.
sites.matters_to: People who follow exploration; people who care about the Moon's future biosphere.
sites.proposed_treatment: Deep undersea community, 4,026 m down (66 atm).
sites.reason: The author's rule for covered sites. The alternative is to move the relics to a shallower community on the South Pole-Aitken Sea coast 80 km away; that is a place-against-depth choice for the author.

sites.name: Chang'e 5
sites.marks: Samples of the Moon's youngest dated basalts, about 2.0 billion years old.

values.historic: The first sample return since 1976.

sites.matters_to: People who follow exploration; planetary scientists.
sites.proposed_treatment: Undersea community, 746 m down.
sites.reason: The author's rule for covered sites.

sites.name: Chang'e 6
sites.marks: The first samples from the far side.

values.historic: Far-side sample return.
values.scientific: Samples of the Apollo basin in South Pole-Aitken.

sites.matters_to: People who follow exploration; planetary scientists.
sites.proposed_treatment: Deep undersea community, 3,311 m down (54 atm).
sites.reason: The author's rule for covered sites; the same depth-against-place choice as Chang'e 4.

sites.name: Chandrayaan-3, Shiv Shakti point
sites.marks: The first landing near the south pole.

values.historic: Opened the polar regions to landers.
values.scientific: The first measurements of polar regolith temperature in place.
values.social: The landing point carries the name Shiv Shakti, with its own cultural meaning.

sites.place_dependence: High. The named point is part of its meaning.
sites.matters_to: People who follow exploration; people for whom the name carries meaning.
sites.proposed_treatment: Land heritage site with an enclosed core in the south-polar highlands.
sites.reason: It stays dry, 2,332 m above the sea.
sites.consult: Heritage specialists; people for whom the name carries meaning.

sites.name: SLIM
sites.marks: A pinpoint landing within about 100 m of its target.

values.historic: Precision landing.
values.social: It landed on its nose and still worked through several lunar nights.

sites.survives: The lander, resting on its nose.
sites.matters_to: People who follow exploration.
sites.proposed_treatment: Land heritage site with an enclosed core, 10 km from the sea.
sites.reason: It stays dry, 416 m above the sea.

sites.name: IM-1 Odysseus
sites.marks: The first commercial landing.

values.historic: A new kind of mission.
values.aesthetic: It carried artworks, among them Jeff Koons' Moon Phases.

sites.survives: The lander, on its side, with the artworks.
sites.matters_to: People who follow exploration; the artists and their audiences.
sites.proposed_treatment: Land heritage site with an enclosed core near Malapert.
sites.reason: It stays dry, 4,480 m above the sea.

sites.name: Blue Ghost 1
sites.marks: A commercial landing that carried the newest laser reflector.

values.historic: A fully successful commercial mission.
values.scientific: Its reflector began a new ranging series in 2025.

sites.matters_to: People who follow exploration; the ranging community.
sites.proposed_treatment: Relic chamber or small undersea community, 2,232 m down; the ranging function moves to high ground.
sites.reason: Covered by the sea.

sites.name: Beresheet crash site
sites.marks: The first privately funded landing attempt.

values.historic: A new kind of mission.
values.social: It carried the Lunar Library archive, designed to last, and dehydrated tardigrades.

sites.survives: Crash debris, possibly the archive discs.
sites.matters_to: People who follow exploration; the archive's makers.
sites.proposed_treatment: Survey for the archive discs before flooding, keep what is found, and mark the site on the sea.
sites.reason: The archive is the lasting part; the crash scattered the craft.

sites.name: Lunar Prospector impact, Shoemaker's ashes
sites.marks: The only human remains on the Moon: about an ounce of Eugene Shoemaker's ashes, scattered at impact.

values.memorial: A resting place for a founder of planetary science.
values.social: The Navajo Nation objected at the time, because the Moon is sacred in Dine tradition.

sites.survives: Debris and ashes mixed into the crater floor.
sites.matters_to: His family and colleagues; the Dine and others who hold the Moon sacred.
sites.proposed_treatment: Marked scattering site; the impact zone is left out of the polar ice excavation; the crater becomes a lake.
sites.reason: The customary care for scattered ashes: respect and marking, with no exclusive claim on the crater.
sites.consult: His family; the Dine; heritage specialists.

sites.name: LCROSS impact, Cabeus
sites.marks: The impact that measured water in a permanently shadowed crater.

values.scientific: The first direct measurement of polar ice and other volatiles.

sites.place_dependence: Low; the crater is the scientific site.
sites.matters_to: Planetary scientists.
sites.proposed_treatment: Marked; part of the Cabeus sampling programme.
sites.reason: Its value is the record in the crater.

sites.name: Hakuto-R Mission 1 crash site
sites.marks: An early commercial landing attempt.

values.historic: A new kind of mission.

sites.matters_to: People who follow exploration.
sites.proposed_treatment: Documented and marked; relics recovered where found.
sites.reason: The crash scattered the craft.

sites.name: Luna 25 crash site
sites.marks: A landing attempt near the south pole.

values.historic: A return attempt after 47 years.

sites.survives: Crash debris and a fresh crater.
sites.matters_to: People who follow exploration.
sites.proposed_treatment: Documented and marked; relics recovered where found.
sites.reason: The crash scattered the craft.

sites.name: Resilience crash site
sites.marks: A commercial landing attempt in Mare Frigoris.

values.historic: A second attempt by the same team.

sites.matters_to: People who follow exploration.
sites.proposed_treatment: Documented and marked; relics recovered where found.
sites.reason: The crash scattered the craft.
